key_insight: Conditioning a 3D generator on an initial 3D shape (using a VecSet-based conditioning mechanism) turns generation into a regeneration task—enabling targeted enhancement, reconstruction, and editing of 3D geometry rather than one-shot synthesis.
problem_solved: One-shot 3D generators offer limited controllability and poor support for refining or editing existing geometry; this paper addresses how to regenerate higher-quality or task-specific 3D objects from 2D images and an initial 3D shape.
method: Introduce a conditional 3D regenerator that takes an initial 3D shape plus optional 2D images as inputs and outputs a refined 3D geometry.
Use VecSet-based conditioning to encode set-structured inputs (e.g., shape tokens, image features) into the generator, enabling flexible conditioning on arbitrary initial shapes.
Unify multiple tasks (enhancement, reconstruction, editing) within the same regeneration pipeline so the model can iteratively refine or modify geometry under different controls.
impact: Provides practitioners a controllable, reusable 3D pipeline for improving and editing existing models from images and partial shapes—useful for AR/VR, simulation, content creation, and downstream vision tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Initial 3D shape + 2D image → VecSet encoder → conditional regenerator → regenerated 3D (flow arrows and brief labels).
Before/After gallery: side-by-side meshes or point clouds showing enhancement, reconstruction, and an edit example.
Task grid: three panels illustrating the three supported tasks (enhancement, reconstruction, editing) with short captions.
VecSet schematic: simple diagram showing set inputs (shape tokens, image features) aggregated into conditioning vectors feeding the generator.
paper_authors: Geon Yeong Park, Roman Shapovalov, Rakesh Ranjan, Jong Chul Ye, Andrea Vedaldi
